data.name: Norway
data.summary: High-tax for investment wealth: dividends and share gains effectively 37.84%, plus a broad worldwide net wealth tax of 1.0-1.1% (about 0.8-0.88% on listed shares after the 20% valuation discount). No inheritance or gift tax, but heirs inherit the cost basis. A 37.84% exit tax on latent share gains above NOK 3m applies on leaving. No special regime for wealthy arrivals. A personal holding AS defers tax: gains on Norwegian/EEA shares and funds are exempt in the company and dividends taxed at 0.66%, with 37.84% due on payout.

regimes.name: Ordinary tax residence
regimes.description: Norwegian tax resident taxed on worldwide income and wealth.
regimes.eligibility: Tax resident if in Norway more than 183 days in any 12-month period or more than 270 days in any 36-month period.

capital_gains.summary: Gains on shares (Norwegian and foreign, listed or unlisted) are multiplied by 1.72 and taxed at the 22% rate on ordinary income, an effective 37.84% (after a small annual shielding deduction on the cost basis). Gains on real estate other than the qualifying main home are taxed at 22%.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: Shielding deduction (skjermingsfradrag): cost basis x a risk-free rate set annually (3.6% for 2025 per the Finance Ministry; the 2026 rate is published in January 2027) is deducted from dividends and, if unused, carried forward. Main home: gain is tax-free if owned and lived in for at least one of the last two years (general rule; not separately re-verified here). A share savings account (aksjesparekonto) defers tax on listed shares/equity funds held inside it until withdrawal of more than the deposits.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Applies to all Norwegian tax residents on worldwide gains.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: EXIT TAX (skatteloven § 10-70, rewritten by Lovvedtak 17 (2024-2025), in force for emigrations from 20 March 2024): on ceasing to be resident, latent gains on shares are taxed as if realised the day before departure, at 37.84%, on the part of total net latent gains above NOK 3,000,000. Payment can be deferred up to 12 years (interest-free 1/12 per year, or a lump sum at the end with interest), with security; deferral ends on realisation, death and certain transfers; the tax lapses for shares still held if the person becomes Norwegian resident again within 12 years. This is a material cost for a family that may later leave Norway. Losses on gains: deductible only where a gain would be taxable.

capital_gains.rate_basis: Share gains: 22% x 1.72 uplift factor = 37.84% (Skatteetaten 2026 table). Same for foreign shares and for a privately held company sold by a personal shareholder. Real estate: 22% ordinary income rate, no uplift. Shielding deduction ignored (small relative to a large gain).
capital_gains.professional_trader: Personal share trading remains capital income under the shareholder model; recharacterisation as business income is uncommon for securities. Not separately researched.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: No holding-period relief; gains taxed in full regardless of holding period.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide taxation; foreign tax credit for tax paid abroad.

dividends.summary: Dividends from Norwegian and foreign companies are multiplied by 1.72 and taxed at 22%, an effective 37.84%, after the shielding deduction. Foreign withholding tax is credited.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: Shielding deduction = cost basis x annual risk-free rate (3.6% for 2025; 2026 rate set January 2027).

open_questions: The 2027 budget proposal (7 October 2026) keeps the 1.72 factor; not yet adopted by the Storting.
dividends.rate_basis: 22% x 1.72 = 37.84% on dividends above the shielding deduction (Skatteetaten 2026).
dividends.withholding_outbound: 25% domestic WHT on dividends to non-residents, reduced by treaty; corporate shareholders resident in the EEA with real substance can be exempt.
dividends.treaty_network: About 82 bilateral treaties plus the Nordic multilateral treaty (PwC table). Treaty with the US in force.
dividends.holding_company_notes: Modelled as the 'holding_as' structure regime: a personal holding company (AS) defers personal dividend and gains tax under the participation exemption (fritaksmetoden) until distribution; distributions then bear 37.84%. Exit tax rules also tie dividends from such shares to repayment of deferred exit tax.

wealth_tax.summary: Broad net wealth tax on worldwide net assets: combined municipal + state rate 1.0% on net wealth above NOK 1,900,000 (single) and 1.1% above NOK 21,500,000. Shares (listed and unlisted, Norwegian and foreign) and equity funds are valued at 80% of market value; a primary home at 25% of estimated market value (70% above NOK 14 million); secondary homes at full value.
wealth_tax.exemptions_thresholds: Allowance NOK 1,900,000 per person (NOK 3,800,000 for spouses taxed jointly). Upper bracket from NOK 21,500,000 net wealth (doubled for spouses).
wealth_tax.regional_differences: Rate split 2026: municipal 0.35%, state 0.65%/0.75%; the combined rate is the same everywhere.
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: Valuation discounts (2026, Skatteetaten): shares including business property 20%, operating assets 30%, primary residence 75% (30% on value above NOK 14 million), secondary residence 0%. Debt attributable to discounted assets is reduced proportionally. For a portfolio of listed shares the effective rate is therefore about 0.8% (1.0% x 0.8) or 0.88% above the upper threshold.
open_questions: 2027 budget proposal (7 October 2026): allowance raised to NOK 1,990,000 (NOK 3,980,000 spouses), rates and 20% share discount unchanged. Not yet adopted; source is a secondary summary.
NOU 2026:9 (tax commission) proposed removing valuation discounts and lowering rates; a study only, not law in force.

components.name: Formuesskatt (municipal + state)
components.notes: Amounts per single taxpayer, doubled for spouses. The 1.1% rate starts at NOK 21,500,000 net wealth, i.e. NOK 19,600,000 above the allowance. Base is after valuation discounts: listed shares and funds count at 80%, primary home at 25% (30% discount above NOK 14m).

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipalities may levy an optional eiendomsskatt on real property; this is not a wealth tax. Rates not researched.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance or gift tax since 1 January 2014. Heirs and donees take over the deceased's or donor's cost basis (continuity), so latent capital gains pass to the children and are taxed when they sell.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Continuity of cost basis means the 37.84% share gain tax is deferred, not forgiven. Exit tax can be triggered if a child emigrates holding inherited shares with latent gains above NOK 3m.
inheritance.gift_tax: None. Gifts carry over the donor's cost basis.

regimes.name: Personal holding company (holding AS) under the participation exemption
regimes.description: The family holds its portfolio through a Norwegian private limited company (aksjeselskap) owned by the parents. Under the participation exemption (fritaksmetoden, skatteloven § 2-38) the company pays no tax on gains on qualifying shares and only 0.66% on qualifying dividends; personal tax of 37.84% is deferred until money is paid out to the family. Qualifying shares are shares in Norwegian and EEA companies and EEA funds (UCITS); direct holdings below 10% in companies outside the EEA (e.g. US shares) do NOT qualify and are taxed at 22% in the company, so the foreign portfolio is normally held via EEA-domiciled funds or EEA shares. Wealth tax and the absence of inheritance tax are as for personal holding (inherited from the standard regime): the AS shares are valued at the company's net tax value with the same 20% share discount.
regimes.eligibility: Any Norwegian tax resident can set up an AS (minimum share capital NOK 30,000). No activity or substance test for the participation exemption on Norwegian/EEA shares held by a Norwegian company. US citizens are excluded here: the US taxes them on the company's passive income under PFIC/CFC rules, which removes the deferral.
regimes.duration_note: Statutory company-tax rules with no time limit; the deferral lasts as long as profits stay in the company and the family stays Norwegian resident (see exit tax).

structure.entity: Holding company (aksjeselskap, AS) owned by the parents
structure.payout_notes: Dividends from the AS to a resident individual are multiplied by 1.72 and taxed at 22% = 37.84%, after the shielding deduction (cost basis of the AS shares x risk-free rate). Loans from the AS to a personal shareholder or close relatives are taxed as dividends (skatteloven § 10-11 fourth paragraph, since 7 October 2015), so borrowing from the company is not a way out. Repayment of paid-in share capital and premium is tax-free. Salary to family members is ordinary earned income.
structure.substance_and_anti_avoidance: No substance or CFC issue for a Norwegian AS owned by Norwegian residents. Key limits: the non-EEA portfolio exception (direct US shares/funds below 10% are taxable at 22%, BFU 5/2026); low-tax-country exclusions; the general anti-avoidance rule (skatteloven § 13-2). The AS must keep accounts and file a company return; with a balance sheet of this size the small-company audit exemption (which has a balance-sheet limit) is unlikely to apply, so an auditor is likely needed (thresholds not re-verified). Moving an existing personal portfolio into the AS is a taxable realisation at 37.84% for the parents, so the structure works best for fresh money or assets with small latent gains on arrival (Norway gives no step-up on immigration).
structure.exit_and_liquidation: Liquidation proceeds are a taxable realisation of the AS shares at 37.84% on the gain. If the parents leave Norway, the exit tax (skatteloven § 10-70) taxes latent gains on the AS shares above NOK 3 million at 37.84%, with deferral up to 12 years. The company is not subject to wealth tax; the parents pay wealth tax on the AS shares, valued at the company's tax value of net assets on 1 January of the income year, less the 20% share discount.

capital_gains.summary: Gains realised by the holding AS on qualifying shares (Norwegian and EEA companies, EEA UCITS/securities funds) are fully exempt under fritaksmetoden, whatever the size of the stake; losses on them are not deductible. Gains on shares in companies resident outside the EEA are exempt only if the AS has held at least 10% of capital and votes for two years, so portfolio gains on e.g. US-listed shares or US funds are taxed at 22% in the company. Gains on real estate owned by the company are taxed at 22%.
capital_gains.exemptions_thresholds: No size threshold for Norwegian and EEA shares. Non-EEA: 10% of capital and votes held continuously for two years before the sale (portfolio exception, skatteloven § 2-38 third paragraph letter b). Shares in low-tax countries outside the EEA never qualify; EEA low-tax companies need real establishment and genuine economic activity.
capital_gains.eligibility_conditions: Shareholder must be a company within § 2-38 first paragraph (an AS qualifies). From 2026 the definition of securities fund sits in FSFIN § 2-38-1; EEA UCITS and equivalent Norwegian funds are treated as companies inside the EEA.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Binding ruling BFU 5/2026 (3 July 2026): units in a US equity fund held by a Norwegian company fall under the portfolio exception and are taxable; the 10% ownership test applies to foreign fund units. A globally diversified portfolio therefore has to be held through EEA-domiciled funds (e.g. Irish or Luxembourg UCITS ETFs) or EEA shares to get the 0% rate; direct US shares are taxed at 22% (still below the 37.84% personal rate, and losses on them are deductible).

open_questions: The JSON assumes the foreign portfolio is held through EEA shares or EEA UCITS funds (0%). If US shares are held directly, the company rate on those gains is 22%.
Treatment of a private business held through the AS assumes a Norwegian or EEA company (exempt).
capital_gains.rate_basis: Fritaksmetoden exempts 100% of gains on qualifying shares (PwC, Corporate income determination). Foreign listed securities set at 0 on the assumption that foreign exposure is held via EEA shares/EEA UCITS funds, which qualify; direct non-EEA holdings below 10% would be 0.22. Private business: 0 for a Norwegian/EEA company held by the AS. Real estate: ordinary 22% corporate income tax.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Company share trading is covered by the participation exemption in the same way; no trader recharacterisation issue for qualifying shares.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: No holding period for Norwegian/EEA shares. Non-EEA shares: 10% stake held for two years.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Worldwide company taxation; foreign tax on taxable income (e.g. non-EEA portfolio gains/dividends) credited.

dividends.summary: Dividends from qualifying shares (Norwegian and EEA companies and funds) are 97% exempt: 3% is taxed at 22%, an effective 0.66%. Dividends from portfolio holdings below 10% in non-EEA companies (e.g. US shares) are fully taxable at 22% with credit for foreign withholding tax. Personal dividend tax of 37.84% arises only when the AS pays out.
dividends.exemptions_thresholds: 3% of qualifying dividends taxed at 22%. Dividends within a tax group (over 90% ownership) fully exempt.
dividends.eligibility_conditions: As for gains: Norwegian/EEA shares and funds qualify regardless of stake; non-EEA shares need 10% (holding period can be met after the dividend date).
dividends.important_exceptions: Foreign dividend withholding (e.g. 15% US treaty WHT, or US WHT suffered inside an Irish fund) is largely lost: the Norwegian tax on a qualifying dividend is only 0.66%, so there is little to credit it against.

open_questions: Whether a credit for foreign withholding can be set against the tax on the 3% portion was not verified; the JSON uses no credit (conservative, immaterial amounts).
dividends.rate_basis: 3% x 22% = 0.66% on qualifying dividends (PwC). Foreign rate assumes EEA shares/EEA funds; direct non-EEA portfolio dividends would be 22% with credit.
dividends.withholding_outbound: As standard: 25% WHT on dividends to non-resident shareholders, reduced by treaty.
dividends.holding_company_notes: This regime models the holding AS itself.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if present more than 183 days in a 12-month period or more than 270 days in a 36-month period. Residence ends from the first income year with no more than 61 days in Norway and no dwelling available to the person or close relatives; after 10+ years of residence, these conditions must be met for three consecutive years (residence ends 1 January of the fourth year).

routes.name: EU/EEA free movement (registration)
routes.requirements: EU/EEA citizens register with UDI/police within three months; non-working persons must show sufficient funds and health insurance. Not verified from UDI (page inaccessible).

routes.name: Work, family or study permit
routes.requirements: Norway has no investor or residence-by-investment visa. Non-EEA nationals need a permit based on work (skilled worker), self-employment, family ties or study. Not verified from UDI in this research.

corporate.summary: 22% corporate income tax (25% for certain financial companies). Participation exemption (fritaksmetoden) for company shareholders; details of its partial clawback not re-verified. 25% WHT on dividends to non-residents, reduced by treaty.
corporate.special_zones: Svalbard has its own low-tax regime (not researched).

income.name: Norway

income_tax.summary: 22% on general income plus bracket tax (trinnskatt) of 1.7% to 17.8% on personal income, plus national insurance 7.6% for employees (10.8% self-employed). Top marginal rate 47.4% for employees (22 + 17.8 + 7.6).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Trygdeavgift for self-employed (other business income) is 10.8% in 2026 per Skatteetaten (PwC's page still shows 11% without a year). Employees 7.6%. No contribution on personal income below NOK 99,650 and the contribution is limited to 25% of income above it.
income_tax.local_tax_note: The 22% general-income rate already includes county, municipal and state elements, so no extra municipal surtax. Bracket thresholds are applied to gross personal income; the 22% is levied after the NOK 114,550 allowance and the minimum deduction (46%, max NOK 95,700), which brackets here do not model.

income.residence_routes: EU/EEA citizens register their residence and may work. Third-country citizens (including US) need a skilled-worker or similar permit tied to an employer; Norway has no digital nomad visa (not verified on an official page).
